meta.title: Case Study: EGM – Institute for Electrochemistry
meta.description: New bilingual website for the EGM Institute for Electrochemistry: conceived, designed and developed by VisionIT.

hero.title: Electrochemistry, made understandable.
hero.description: New website for EGM, the Institute for Electrochemistry, Electroplating and Materials Chemistry: conceived, designed and developed by VisionIT.

intro.label: 01 — Starting point
intro.title: Deep expertise, hard to grasp.
paragraphs: EGM is a state-authorised and sworn civil engineering institute with more than 20 years of industry practice – court-certified experts in chemistry, corrosion and surface technology.

Eleven specialist services, six focus areas and very different audiences – from industrial companies to courts, lawyers and insurers – had to come together on one website, without anyone needing a chemistry degree.

elektrochemie.screenshotAlt: Hero of the elektrochemie.eu homepage with a holographic background

work.label: 02 — Implementation
work.title: Six elements, one reaction.
work.description: Inspired by the periodic table, every part of the project became its own element – just like the competences on the finished website.

items.title: Concept
items.description: Information architecture for eleven services, six focus areas, expert reports and the team – with clear paths instead of a maze of jargon.

items.title: Questions as the way in
items.description: “How can we help you?” – eight concrete questions meet visitors at their problem and lead straight to the right service.

items.title: Design in logo colours
items.description: Blue, cyan and violet from the EGM logo, element tiles as a recurring motif and a holographic hero that makes surfaces and reactions visible.

items.title: Expert reports in focus
items.description: A dedicated area for courts, lawyers, insurers and private reports – with a direct call to action for report requests.

items.title: Bilingual
items.description: German and English with a dedicated language switch – for international industrial clients and specialist conferences.

items.title: Development & launch
items.description: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Tailwind CSS – fast, responsive and from frontend to deployment from a single source.

result.label: 03 — Result
result.title: A presence as precise as the work behind it.

meta.title: Case Study: HerzHirnHumor – Psychotherapy
meta.description: A calm, trustworthy website for a psychotherapy practice in Vienna – with online booking in three languages.

hero.illustrationLabel: Line drawing: heart and brain, connected by a smile
hero.titleStart: A website with heart, brain and
hero.description: Website for the psychotherapy practice of Maram Maria Zyadeh, MA in Vienna – calm, trustworthy and so clear that the first step feels easier.

herzhirnhumor.screenshotAlt: Homepage of herzhirnhumor.at with a line illustration and hero text

challenge.label: The challenge
challenge.title: People looking for therapy are often going through a difficult time.
challenge.description: So the website has to radiate calm, build trust and answer the most important questions before they are asked: How does therapy work? What does it cost? And how do I get a first appointment?

items.title: Calm design
items.description: Warm cream and sage tones, plenty of white space, light typography and a fine line illustration as a signature – nothing that pushes.

items.title: Three-step process
items.description: Contact, first conversation, next steps: the path into therapy is clear at a glance and eases the uncertainty before the first call.

items.title: Transparent terms
items.description: Fees, cost subsidies, cancellation policy, confidentiality and therapy duration – communicated openly instead of hidden in small print.

items.title: Direct booking
items.description: Quick online appointments right from the navigation, plus contact form, phone and address – everyone finds the right way in.

items.title: Visible emergency contacts
items.description: Crisis hotlines have a permanent place on the site – a responsibility that simply belongs on a health website.

items.title: Three languages
items.description: German, English and French – matching a practice that offers therapy in all three languages.

meta.title: Case Study: Camp Currie – Community Farm
meta.description: An inviting website for a community farm for sustainable agriculture in Upper Austria – from Figma design to deployment.

hero.title: Camp Currie
hero.description: A website for a community farm for sustainable agriculture in Upper Austria.

facts.label: MY ROLE
facts.value: Concept, design in Figma, development, deployment

intro.label: The starting point
intro.title: Plenty of life on the farm – and plenty to tell.
paragraphs: Camp Currie is a certified organic community farm in the Mühlviertel: fields, animals, shared work and people who want to get involved. All of that needed a place on one website – without it feeling overloaded.
The goal was an inviting, clearly structured presence that conveys the project's values and shows interested people how they can take part.

campCurrie.screenshotAlt: Homepage of camp-currie.at with a landscape image and the Camp Currie lettering

items.title: Design in Figma
items.description: Designed and agreed in Figma first: bold Anton headlines, handwritten accents, natural tones in sage green and harvest yellow.

items.title: An atmospheric opening
items.description: A large landscape image of the farm welcomes visitors – you immediately feel what it's about.

items.title: Clear structure
items.description: About us, farm, animals, organic certification, getting involved, news and contact – one continuous page with clear navigation.

items.title: Getting involved made easy
items.description: A dedicated section and frequently asked questions show interested people how they can take part.

items.title: News from the farm
items.description: A news slider with harvest previews, new animal arrivals and farm offers keeps the site alive.

items.title: Gallery & partners
items.description: An image gallery shows everyday life on the farm, and partners get their own place.

meta.title: Case Study: Pictolog PDF – own app
meta.description: An offline app that turns photos and notes into clean photo documentation – independently conceived, designed and developed.

hero.description: An offline app that turns photos and notes into clean photo documentation in just a few steps – independently conceived, designed and developed.

idea.label: The idea
idea.title: Photos are quick to take. The documentation isn't.
paragraphs: Anyone recording progress, conditions or work collects photos in the gallery – and then laboriously copies them into a document. Pictolog cuts that down to three steps, right on the phone.
Because photos are often sensitive, one thing was clear from the start: everything stays local on the device. No account, no cloud, and it works without a connection.

steps.title: Create and name a project
steps.description: Title and description automatically end up on the PDF's cover page.

steps.title: Add photos as pages
steps.description: Directly with the camera or from the gallery – each page with its own description.

steps.title: Create and share the PDF
steps.description: Check the preview, save as PDF or pass it on directly via the share menu.

features.label: Features & implementation
features.title: Small in scope, careful in detail.

items.title: Offline-first
items.description: Local data storage with Hive – no account, no cloud.

items.title: Custom camera view
items.description: Take photos right in the app or choose them from the gallery.

items.title: Edit pages
items.description: Rotate, replace and describe images, and reorder them by drag & drop.

items.title: PDF generation
items.description: Cover page, image pages with descriptions and a footer – generated right on the device.

items.title: Light, dark, system
items.description: Full dark mode with its own colour system and checked contrasts.

items.title: German & English
items.description: Localised including plural forms, with language switching in the app.

meta.title: Case Study: splitn – share expenses fairly
meta.description: An app for couples, flatmates and groups of friends with fair splitting and clear balances – idea, design, app and backend from a single source.

hero.description: An app for couples, flatmates and groups of friends who shop and spend together – with fair splitting and clear balances. Idea, design, app and backend from a single source.

idea.label: The idea
idea.title: Shopping together is easy. Settling up fairly isn't.
paragraphs: Whether it's a couple, a flatshare or a holiday with friends: not every expense is split equally. Sometimes one person pays for everything, sometimes it's split by percentage or individually – and in the end nobody knows who owes whom what.
splitn calculates each share according to the split type, keeps balances per group and shows at a glance who has to pay and who gets something back.

items.description: Classic half and half – the fastest way for everyday life.
Full amount: one person covers everything, the other owes it.
Percent: adjust the split with a slider.
Custom: enter amounts per person – with a live display of what's still open.

items.title: Groups & balances
items.description: Active balances per member, “Settle all debts” with one tap.

items.title: Friends via QR code
items.description: Your own QR code to share and scan instead of cumbersome invitations.

items.title: Push notifications
items.description: Can be switched on and off in the app at any time.

items.title: Account & privacy
items.description: Login, profile with picture, default currency – and account deletion that keeps everyone else's balances correct.

items.title: German & English
items.description: Fully localised, with language selection in the app.
